findings.description: The generated Agent Teams constraint block in `CLAUDE.loa.md` was not regenerated after the corresponding rationales changed in `.claude/data/constraints.json`. The file still contains the old shorter rationale text and the old generated hash (`c020-teamcreate`) for `agent_teams_constraints`.
findings.failure_mode: Generated instruction artifacts drift from their source of truth. Any validation that checks generated constraint blocks against `.claude/data/constraints.json` will fail, and agents consuming `CLAUDE.loa.md` receive stale rationale text despite the source update.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate `CLAUDE.loa.md` from `.claude/data/constraints.json` so the `agent_teams_constraints` block text and hash match the updated source, or revert the source rationale edits if they were not intended to affect generated instructions.

findings.description: Sprint AC 'Replay A/B: no gold case loses recall' is not met by the change under review. The pre-registered gate (pooled n=9, after >= before per case, fixed before extra trials ran) failed on five cases: review-pr-02 .926->.815, review-pr-05 .963->.852, audit-pr-02 .852->.815, audit-pr-03 1->.963, audit-pr-05 .926->.889. Missed-defect slots doubled from 5/144 to 10/144, concentrated on D13-find-exec-multi-root (0/6 -> 3/6) and D06-prerelease-tags-rejected (1/6 -> 3/6). The pre-registered remedy (revert or retune the implicated change) was not applied; a post-hoc LLM adjudication was substituted as the measure, and even on that measure audit-pr-02 still loses (.963 vs 1.000). The ablation commit c9b7bdc0 restored only this include and left the long-class thresholds table in tool-result-clearing.md, the five protocol moves, and the CLAUDE.loa.md diet in place, so 'the include is not what moves the grader' does not exclude the other diff-touched changes (kernel truenames/Reference collapse, constraint rationale cuts) as the cause; the before arm (main 2079e719) has none of them.
findings.failure_mode: reviewing-code and auditing-security ship with a measured recall regression on the gold set. Defects of the D13 (multi-root find -exec) and D06 (prerelease tag rejection) classes pass the review and audit gates in roughly half of trials instead of 0-1 in 6. The gates are the framework's only check that code meets acceptance and security criteria (per C-PROC rationale in this same diff), so the regression is a production quality exposure, not a test artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the pre-registered gate as binding. Either (a) revert the default to standard thresholds (or the full Sprint 3 diet) until bd-ewrc lands and a re-baselined A/B passes the registered gate on the fixed grader, or (b) run a proper component ablation: after-tree minus include, after-tree minus protocol thresholds table, after-tree minus kernel diet, each at n=9 on the five losing cases, and revert the component that moves recall. Do not accept a post-hoc adjudicated measure as the AC gate; record the decision in the audit, not the implementer report.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff edits the why field of the five C-TEAM constraints (constraints.json hunks at 1232, 1253, 1274, 1295, 1316). The rendered agent_teams_constraints block in CLAUDE.loa.md, which claims to be generated from constraints.json, was not touched by the regeneration and its Why text matches neither the old nor the new why.
findings.description: Five of the twelve tightened rationales have no rendered effect. generate-constraints.sh was re-run and the process_compliance_never/always hashes changed (74e01d57->2fe3c087, bcb45bf9->811c6b84), but the agent_teams_constraints block kept the static non-hash marker 'hash:c020-teamcreate' and Why text such as 'Planning skills assume single-writer semantics' and 'SQLite single-writer prevents lock contention', which match neither the pre- nor post-diff why. Either the block is hand-maintained under a 'DO NOT EDIT - generated from constraints.json' marker, or the generator renders it from a different field. prompt-audit-generated-blocks passed 3/3 with this divergence, so the drift check does not cover the block. The report's 'twelve rationales tightened ... golden tables re-rendered' holds for seven.
findings.failure_mode: Future edits to C-TEAM why strings silently never reach the kernel prompt, and the generated/DO-NOT-EDIT marker gives a false guarantee. Anyone correcting an Agent Teams rationale in constraints.json (e.g. after an incident) will believe the kernel updated when it did not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make generate-constraints.sh render agent_teams_constraints from why (or a declared short-why field) with a real content hash and add the block to the prompt-audit-generated-blocks drift check, or remove the generated marker from that section and revert the five no-op constraints.json edits so the source of truth is not misleading.

findings.description: The include fixes long as the default class, and per the report the SessionStart hook resolves every error path to long. The permissive class is therefore the fail-open outcome for a <=200K model whenever detection fails: payload lacks .model, catalog alias miss, yq absent, or the hook not wired in a consumer repo that only merged one of the two settings files. Long thresholds are 20K single / 50K accumulated / 30K full file / 150K session, i.e. 75% of a 200K window before the extraction rule fires, on top of kernel, skills, and includes.
findings.failure_mode: On a 200K-window session (e.g. Haiku 4.5) with detection failure, the agent follows long-class discipline, never extracts to NOTES.md, exhausts context, and compacts mid-task. The compaction destroys exactly the cross-session state the discipline exists to preserve, and Run Mode Recovery then resumes from a NOTES.md that was never updated.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed: resolve unknown model and error paths to standard, select long only on a positive catalog match >200K or an explicit LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=long, and change the include wording to 'standard when the class is unknown'. Add a CC test for the no-.model / no-catalog path asserting standard.

findings.description: Two pieces of operative guidance were dropped from the include without a skill-reachable replacement. (a) The NOTES.md routing clause 'decisions -> Decision Log, issues -> Technical Debt' is gone; with session-continuity.md moved to .claude/protocols/reference/ behind a stub in this same sprint, the routing rule is now two hops from any skill. (b) The protocol reference shrank from .claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md to the bare tool-result-clearing.md. This sprint created a second protocols directory (protocols/reference/), so a bare name is now ambiguous, and bare names are invisible to protocol-refs-resolve, so a future move of that file would not be caught.
findings.failure_mode: Agents append decisions and debt into Session Continuity or arbitrary sections; notes-guard section reads and Decision Log consumers miss them, and the 'reason from the synthesis' step degrades. A skill loaded without the protocols tree in context may fail to locate the thresholds file by bare name.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full protocol path (19 bytes) and a short routing clause such as 'decisions -> Decision Log, debt -> Technical Debt' (about 45 bytes, within the include's headroom), or move the routing rule into the NOTES.md template header where notes-guard surfaces it on every read.
